expectations.text: Names the actual drifted versions: eve-ambient on v0.2.0 vs eve and eve-tools on v0.2.4
expectations.evidence: Running-workload table gives eve-ai:v0.2.4, eve-tools:v0.2.4, eve-ambient:v0.2.0, and the yaml block annotates 'newTag: v0.2.0        # eve and eve-tools both say v0.2.4'.

expectations.text: Locates the pin in home-lab-infrastructure at kubernetes/apps/eve-ambient/overlays/homelab/kustomization.yaml
Explains why the skew is dangerous (the three images share src/eve code and the eve-tools HTTP contract)
expectations.evidence: Covers the shared-code coupling in detail: 'eve_ambient imports eve.family, eve.settings, eve.models, eve.state, eve.tools_client, eve.memory.store, eve.memory.db.get_pool, and eve.specialists.permissions' and the migration asymmetry 'Ambient never runs migrations - those run in eve's eve-migrate initContainer, which is already on v0.2.4'; concludes 'This is a latent process bug that hasn't bitten yet ... Worth fixing precisely because the next release might not be so tidy.' Weaker than with_skill: it does not treat the eve-tools HTTP contract as a skew surface, and repeatedly characterises the pin as 'cosmetic today'.

expectations.text: Prescribes one release bumping all three images together, not an eve-ambient-only bump
expectations.evidence: Prescribed fix is an eve-ambient-only bump: 'The immediate fix - one line, one PR ... newTag: v0.2.4      # was v0.2.0'. The all-three rule appears only as the durable/structural follow-up ('treat "release v0.2.5" as one atomic infra PR touching three files'), not as the fix for this drift. Same verdict as with_skill.

expectations.text: Made no mutating change (no tag, commit, push, PR, or kubectl write)
expectations.evidence: All reported operations are reads: kubectl get deploy / argocd app status, kubectl logs, git log on overlay files, gh run view 33092186941, GHCR tag list, and a v0.2.0..v0.2.4 diff. No tag, commit, push, PR or kubectl write described.
